newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Greenpeace to inspect Taiwan nuclear waste site.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace to inspect Taiwan nuclear waste site.

text.p: The environment group Greenpeace said on Monday it will oppose Taiwan's plan to ship up to 200,000 barrels of low-radiation nuclear waste to North Korea during a visit to the island next month.
"We plan to inspect the nuclear waste site on Lanyu island (from which the shipment will be sent) around May 8," Greenpeace activist Ho Wai-chi told Reuters.
Lanyu, an islet southeast of Taiwan, is where state utility Taipower stores its nuclear waste.

Residents on the island have fiercely opposed the waste site, and Taipower promises to clear the 100,000 barrels of nuclear waste buried on the island by the year 2000. In January, the state utility signed a contract with North Korea to ship 200,000 barrels of the waste there.

Ho said Greenpeace would hold a conference on the issue in Taipei on May 17 with experts from the United States, Japan, Sweden and Taiwan. The aim was to make people in Taiwan more aware of the problem and question the need for nuclear energy.
He said it was wrong and dangerous to ship one's own nuclear waste to another country.
